title: A missed train cleaning exposed a dispute over access to BART witnesses

beats.text: Why did BART’s graffiti safety investigation end before inspectors saw a crew clean a train?

visual.sub: A safety inquiry ended without access to the crew

beats.text: The office counted 15 vandalism incidents without a cleaning notice.

visual.label: A safety inquiry ended without access to the crew

beats.text: A planned Sunday visit fell through. Time records put the cleaning on Monday.
Nine attempts to reach three workers drew no reply.

visual.label: A safety inquiry ended without access to the crew

beats.text: The union objected to the contacts. The workers were witnesses.
In 2024, union leaders and the inspector marked up a draft charter.

visual.kicker: The committee preserved the competing proposals in writing

beats.text: They disagreed on who should notify the union before an interview.
In 2026, a civil grand jury reported a separate executive interview dispute.

visual.kicker: A second, separate dispute involved an executive

beats.text: BART said the executive answered in writing and the retaliation allegation was not sustained.
The board voted nine to zero to send its response.

visual.label: The board approved a response, with policy adoption still pending in that response

beats.text: It said a cooperation policy still required labor review.
The original report left the safety of the cleaning procedure unresolved.
Every source is linked in the case file below.
